description: SPS unveiled a Missing Person's Gallery at headquarters.
SPS hosted an Explorer recruiting event for young women.
SPS launched its annual Citizen Police Perception Survey.

chips.text: Camp Caterpillar receives proceeds from the annual Pride BBQ.
SPS hosted a calling home ceremony for MMIWG families.

description: Police presented statistics on drivers fleeing peace officers.
Air support unit interventions decreased due to pilot and mechanical issues.

chips.text: Chief McBride explained pilot shortages and mechanical issues reduced air support unit flight time.
Reasons for drivers evading police were not broken down by specific criminal act.
New pilot for air support unit is in training, expected operational by mid-Summer.

speakers.name: Nolan Berg
speakers.summary: Nolan Berg presented the report and responded to questions of the Board, along with Chief McBride.
said: Report details review process and statistics of flight from peace officer incidents.
Incidents with no pursuit increased; incidents with pursuit remained consistent.
Pursuits are terminated when public risk becomes too high.

description: Saskatoon Police use of force decreased in 2025.
Force was used in 0.17% of calls.
Public Safety Unit made 3 arrests without force.

chips.text: Commissioner Greyeyes noted 0.17% use of force addresses common misconceptions.

speakers.name: Cory Goodwin
speakers.summary: Cory Goodwin presented the report and responded to questions of the Board.
said: The report reflects the service's management and oversight of use of force.
Force was used in 0.17% of calls in 2025, a 26% decrease from 2024.
Public Safety Unit deployed 110 times in 2025 with no force applied.

description: City police find tracking PACT team availability challenging.
PACT teams primarily respond to mental health crises.
Unavailability of PACT teams increases police response to incidents.

chips.text: Commissioner Grier noted PACT teams are not fully funded by the province.
Individuals experiencing mental health crises rely on PACT team availability.
Chief McBride offered to analyze dispatch data comparing PACT responses to mental health calls.
